title: Shared reading lists
subtitle: Owners share a reading list by email; invited readers open it read-only, and every list read now goes through the access rules.

cards.title: Shared list page
cards.summary: Shows a list to its owner or an invited reader; anyone else is denied.

cards.title: Share dialog
cards.summary: Owner enters an email to invite a reader.

cards.title: Share endpoint
cards.summary: Validates the owner and the email, then creates an invite.

cards.title: List endpoint
cards.summary: Returns a list only to users with a role on it.

cards.title: Invitations
cards.summary: Issues hashed, expiring tokens and accepts them once.

cards.title: Access rules
cards.summary: Owner, reader or no access, for every read.

cards.title: List repository
cards.summary: List queries, now with reader membership.

cards.title: Invite repository

cards.summary: Sends the invitation email from a template.

src/components/share-dialog.tsx.role: Form that sends an invitation by email and reports a failed send.

src/db/migrations/0007_invites.sql.role: Adds the invites table with a hashed, unique token.

src/api/lists/get.ts.role: List endpoint, now behind the access rules.

src/domain/access.ts.role: Decides whether a user owns, reads or cannot see a list.

src/db/lists.ts.role: Queries for lists, including reader membership.

src/infra/mailer.ts.role: Transactional email with a template per message.

notes.text: Loads the list through the access check and renders the denied state instead of throwing.
Only owners see the share control; readers get the same page without it.
Posts the invitation and keeps a failed send visible so the owner can retry.
Only the owner may invite; the email is validated before anything is written.
Returns the invite id and expiry, never the token.
The token is random, stored only as a hash, and expires after seven days.
Accepting binds the invite to one user and one list; unknown or expired tokens return null.
Active means not revoked and not expired, checked in the same query.
Every read now goes through the access rules; a missing role becomes the denied state.
Imports the invite repository for revocation.
Readers are a second role; anything else has no access.
Reader membership is derived from accepted, non-revoked invites; there is no second table to keep in sync.

attention.title: An invite token opens exactly one list
attention.scenario: A reader reuses or alters an invitation token to reach another owner's list.
attention.handling: Tokens are random, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, bound to one list and one accepting user, and expire after seven days.

evidence.note: Random token, hashed before storage, with expiry.
Lookup requires not revoked and not expired.

tests.title: invites grants read access to exactly one list

qa: Change one character of a token in the link and check the list does not open.

attention.title: Revoking while an invitation is pending
attention.scenario: The owner revokes a reader while an unaccepted invitation for the same email is still valid.
attention.handling: Revocation marks every open invite of the list as revoked in one statement; accepted readers lose access on the next request.
attention.residual: An invite accepted in the same instant as the revocation can still succeed once; no lock covers both statements.

attention.title: Mail failure after the invite is stored
attention.scenario: The mail provider rejects the message after the invite row was written.
attention.handling: The dialog reports the failure and the owner can retry; the stored invite stays valid but unknown to the reader.

evidence.note: Mail is sent after the insert, outside a transaction.

qa: Stop the mail catcher, share a list, and check the dialog shows the retry message.

attention.title: Invitation flooding
attention.scenario: An owner sends thousands of invitations to unrelated addresses.
